tasks.title: Deploy the whole OneCLI stack (tango) to Railway and make the Eysho/Custom LLM provider usable
changedFiles: railway.json, railway/* (deleted — superseded by the IaC file)
commits: 32ef0b97 fix(gateway): only use /app/data as default data dir when it is writable
a13637dc feat(railway): deploy the tango branch with Railway IaC
a95784b5 fix(railway): drop the Dockerfile VOLUME Railway rejects, harden the deploy script
abcfd83d fix(railway): use the real service names and check them up front
05c0a912 feat(web): single-origin proxy so a split-domain deployment can sign in
810df31c fix(web): the Custom secret dialog must not name OpenAI's host
rootCauses: railway.json used a 'services' map the Railway schema does not know; the web silently fell back to RAILPACK — replaced by the .railway/railway.ts IaC file.
Railway's Docker builder rejects 'VOLUME' in a Dockerfile ('docker VOLUME at Line 67 is not supported, use Railway Volumes') — the gateway image never built.
The web domain pointed at 10254 while the container listened on Railway's injected PORT=8080 → 502 on every request.

up.railway.app is a public suffix (PSL private section): every generated Railway hostname is its own registrable domain, so a session cookie between the dashboard and the api is a third-party cookie that SameSite=Lax never sends — sign-up returned 200 but the UI hung. Fixed with the single-origin proxy (ONECLI_SINGLE_ORIGIN_PROXY=1).
The gateway's default data dir picked /app/data on mere existence; a root-owned /app/data on the host made the first CA write fail with EACCES — now probed for writability.
verification: cargo test -p onecli-gateway --bin onecli-gateway → 3 passed
vitest (apps/web): next-config-single-origin, next-config-redirects, next-config-bake → 18 passed
vitest (apps/web): secret-dialog.test.tsx → 54 passed (incl. the new api.eysho.info wording test)
eslint --max-warnings 0 on the changed web files → clean
curl https://bkg-one-cli-production.up.railway.app/v1/health → 200 (API through the web proxy)
curl https://bkg-one-cli-production.up.railway.app/gw/healthz → 200 (gateway through the web proxy)
curl https://bkg-one-cli-production.up.railway.app/healthz → 200
curl https://api-production-f27ca.up.railway.app/v1/health → 200
curl https://gateway-production-b061.up.railway.app/healthz → 200

browser (agent-browser): account created and sign-in works; Connections → LLMs → Add LLM Key shows Anthropic / OpenAI / Custom; the Custom dialog reads 'Your key is encrypted and injected into requests to api.eysho.info.', name 'Custom Token', host pattern 'api.eysho.info'
blockers: The gateway image compiles the Rust workspace from scratch on Railway (~6-12 min per build).
The prod compose stack under /srv/bkg/services/onecli is down (only postgres runs) — cli.eysho.info answers 404; it was not part of this task.
notes: Shared secrets (BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY, GATEWAY_INTERNAL_SECRET) were never rewritten — a fresh SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY would orphan every encrypted credential.
API_URL / GATEWAY_API_URL stay unset on Railway: the browser must use the dashboard's own origin, the resolver derives api=<origin> and gateway=<origin>/gw.
Another agent session works in the same repo (turbo bump in package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml/turbo.json) — those changes were never staged into these commits.

tasks.title: Make the Custom (Eysho) provider work in the runtime paths, not just in the UI
rootCauses: The provider type 'eysho' was added to the API's provider registry, but the Rust gateway — the component that actually injects credentials into agent traffic — knew only 'anthropic', 'openai' and 'generic'. build_injections('eysho') fell through to the empty arm, so a Custom key was stored, granted and shown in the UI while every agent call to api.eysho.info went out unauthenticated.

llm-direct-call.ts mapped every non-Anthropic credential to the OpenAI shape and origin, so a Custom key resolved as {provider:'openai'} and would have been sent to api.openai.com — a credential leak to a third party.
api.eysho.info was missing from both LLM-host lists (Rust policy::is_llm_host and its TypeScript mirror), so the provider's traffic was not recognized as LLM traffic.
The provider label was 'Eysho' in the API registry and in the secret-type labels, so the dashboard's own surfaces (model card, secret card, grant row) showed 'Eysho' instead of the agreed 'Custom'.
changedFiles: turbo.json (EYSHO_API_BASE_URL in globalPassThroughEnv — own hunk staged, the concurrent turbo schema bump stays unstaged)
commits: fix(llm): the Custom provider must work in the runtime, not just in the UI
verification: cargo test -p inject -p policy → inject 134 passed (incl. 3 new eysho tests), policy 37 passed
cargo fmt --check -p inject -p policy -p proxy → clean
pnpm --filter @onecli/api check-types → clean
pnpm --filter @onecli/api lint → clean
pnpm --filter @onecli/gateway-e2e lint → clean
vitest (packages/api, full suite) → 5359 passed, 0 failed, 1871 skipped
vitest (packages/api, targeted) → llm-direct-call 25, path-match 11, llm-registry 36, secret-service 2, hermetic-env 17 passed
gateway-e2e tests/inject.test.ts → 23 passed, incl. 'injects the Custom provider's key as a Bearer' (real gateway binary, real DB row, real decrypt, upstream saw 'authorization: Bearer sk-proj-e2e')

gateway-e2e full suite → 300 passed / 11 failed; all 11 are the Postgres front-door scenarios and they fail IDENTICALLY with the HEAD binary (git stash + rebuild + rerun) — pre-existing in this environment, not caused by this change
notes: The eysho provider is API-key only: no OAuth arm, and the metadata's authMode is ignored for it.
The Decisions API stays OpenAI-only: answersTyped() is not widened, so a Custom key uses the prompt path with the provider's own fallback model gpt-4o-mini.
Railway auto-deploys on every push to tango, so the push triggers a full rebuild of all four services.

EYSHO_API_BASE_URL is a test-double override like ANTHROPIC_API_BASE_URL / OPENAI_API_BASE_URL; it must stay in the hermetic-env list, in turbo.json's globalPassThroughEnv and out of every ambient shell.

tasks.title: Close the open points of the tango deployment: Custom provider catalog path, egress allowlist semantics, production test artifacts
scope: Railway production (test artifacts: secret, agent, account)
rootCauses: The Custom provider's catalog request was never exercised: the models endpoint serves HOSTED agents only, and the Railway deployment has no runner, so a hosted agent cannot be created there. The provider's own catalog code had no test at all.
eysho.catalogHeaders sent NO authorization header when the auth mode was 'oauth' — a mode the provider does not have. A row whose metadata claimed it would have listed without its key.
The credential's auth mode was read with the OPENAI metadata parser for every non-Anthropic provider, so a Custom row whose metadata said 'oauth' was classified as a subscription login.
eysho.parseCatalog kept a row with an empty id (the other two parsers drop it) and stamped a 'source' field the parser contract does not have.

The deploy script set GATEWAY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DESTINATIONS=true. The egress guard parses that variable as a LIST of hosts/IPs/CIDRs, so 'true' became the hostname 'true': an allow-list that allows nothing, presented as 'allow everything'.
commits: fix(railway,llm): the Custom provider's catalog request, and an honest egress allow-list
verification: vitest (packages/api, full suite) → 5363 passed, 0 failed, 1871 skipped
vitest (packages/api, targeted) → llm-registry 40 passed (incl. 4 new Custom-catalog tests), llm-direct-call 25, path-match 11, hermetic-env 17
pnpm --filter @onecli/api lint → clean; check-types → clean; prettier → clean
bash -n scripts/deploy-railway.sh → ok (shellcheck is not installed here)
deploy script --variables-only → gateway/GATEWAY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DESTINATIONS deleted, every other variable 'already correct' or 'not set'
Railway after the push of bdd61a5b → migrations, api, bkg-one-cli, gateway all SUCCESS; health 200 on web /healthz, web /v1/health, web /gw/healthz, api /v1/health, gateway /healthz
gateway log (deployment 1390ecc1) → 'egress guard: non-public destinations are refused (GATEWAY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DESTINATIONS unset)' ×1, 'BETTER_AUTH_SECRET not set' ×0
browser on the final build → sign-up works, Connections → LLMs → 'Add LLM Key' shows the third option 'Custom — Inject an API key for requests to api.eysho.info'
production cleanup → secret, agent and the test account deleted (HTTP 204 each), a second verification account deleted (204), /v1/auth/session afterwards → 401
notes: The hosted jcode harness routes only to claude / claude-api / codex — there is no route for a third provider, so a HOSTED agent cannot run a turn on the Custom provider yet. The gateway injection and the control plane's direct calls can.
The Railway deployment has no runner service: POST /v1/agents with kind=hosted answers 422 'No runner is available to host this agent.'

No valid Eysho key is available here, and api.eysho.info answers 401 without one — so the LIVE catalog of the real provider is not proven; the request path is proven against a stub and in the unit test.
The compose stack under /srv/bkg/services/onecli was NOT started: no onecli-* images exist on this host and only postgres is running. cli.eysho.info is unchanged (404).
The Railway CLI is now linked to the web service (bkg-one-cli) instead of Postgres, so a stray command without --service cannot touch the database.
